findings.text: deferrals_recorded and its helpers at 169-203 re-implement, as a third reader, the capability that reckon/crew/runs.py:2792 (recorded_promoted_acknowledgements) and reckon/crew/runs.py:3000 (run_acknowledgement) already own, and restate the record shape that reckon/crew/obligations.py:1794 (_acknowledgements_in_force) applies; they duplicate rather than extend the owner. The duplication is forced -- the prompt hook loads this module by path and cannot import reckon.crew -- but it is unguarded against drift: nothing asserts this reader and _acknowledgements_in_force agree on a record, and their project filters already differ (here `record.get('project') or project`, against runs.py:2812 `str(payload.get('project') or '')`), so a future shape moves one without the other. This is the very defect class the repaired commit fixed.

the repair's user-visible half -- a promoted run's deferral keeping the stop from blocking -- is asserted only through the predicate: tests/test_a_promoted_deferral_is_seen_by_the_hook_path.py calls obligation_snapshot.deferrals_recorded directly and never drives reapply_acknowledgements, and tests/test_an_acknowledgement_ends_on_its_condition.py:123 keeps a live pointer carrying the same deferral, so its early return is answered by the live file. A regression in this call (returning payload before consulting deferrals_recorded, or reading another project) leaves every test in the tree green.

the fragment states 'The two alias exports left behind by the render move are gone', but reckon/crew/obligations.py:1296-1297 still assign _render_overdue_remedy and _overdue_figure from the reader; the two names removed at 36e7a0e83c are _age_of_instant and refresh_overdue_remedy. A reader checking whether the alias bridge survives gets the wrong answer from the evidence record.

the recorded arm pair (tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py plus tests/test_every_shared_home_lock_holds_across_nodes.py) imports only reckon.interface_counts and reads the tree by AST census, so it is not the done_when's 'arm over the test files that import what you changed': 58 passed on both sides shows the census still accounts for the new module, not that the changed modules behave. The manifest also records no ruff result on the changed paths, which the done_when requires, and lists commits space-separated where the done_when asks for a comma-separated list.

the payload_for delivery_summary call is re-wrapped across five lines with no behaviour change and no relation to the node's goal (the hook path never calls payload_for, which lives on the crew side); it is formatting noise inside a behavioural commit.
